sentences.text: Adderall is a combination drug containing salts of the two enantiomers of amphetamine , a central nervous system -LRB- CNS -RRB- stimulant of the phenethylamine class .	stimulant	stimulant	combination drug	combination drug	salts	salt (chemistry)	amphetamine	amphetamine	central nervous system	central nervous system	phenethylamine class	substituted phenethylamine	phenethylamine	phenethylamine

Adderall is used in the treatment of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder -LRB- ADHD -RRB- and narcolepsy .	attention deficit hyperactivity disorder	attention deficit hyperactivity disorder	narcolepsy	narcolepsy

It is also used as an athletic performance enhancer and cognitive enhancer , and recreationally as an aphrodisiac and euphoriant .	athletic performance enhancer	Performance-enhancing substance	cognitive enhancer	Nootropic	aphrodisiac	aphrodisiac	euphoriant	euphoriant

By salt content , the active ingredients of Adderall are 25 % levoamphetamine salts -LRB- the levorotary or ` left-handed ' enantiomer -RRB- and 75 % dextroamphetamine salts -LRB- the dextrorotary or ` right-handed ' enantiomer -RRB- .	salts	salt (chemistry)	enantiomer	enantiomer	levoamphetamine	levoamphetamine	levorotary	levorotary	dextroamphetamine	dextroamphetamine	dextrorotary	dextrorotary
Adderall is generally well-tolerated and effective in treating the symptoms of ADHD and narcolepsy .	narcolepsy	narcolepsy

At therapeutic doses , Adderall causes emotional and cognitive effects such as euphoria , change in desire for sex , increased wakefulness , and improved cognitive control .	euphoria	euphoria	desire for sex	libido	wakefulness	wakefulness	cognitive control	Executive functions
At these doses , it induces physical effects such as decreased reaction time , fatigue resistance , and increased muscle strength .

In contrast , much larger doses of Adderall can impair cognitive control , cause rapid muscle breakdown , or induce a psychosis -LRB- e.g. , delusions and paranoia -RRB- .	cognitive control	Executive functions	rapid muscle breakdown	Rhabdomyolysis	psychosis	Stimulant psychosis#Amphetamines

The side effects of Adderall vary widely among individuals , but most commonly include insomnia , dry mouth , and loss of appetite .	insomnia	insomnia	dry mouth	dry mouth	loss of appetite	loss of appetite

The risk of developing an addiction is insignificant when Adderall is used as prescribed at fairly low daily doses , such as those used for treating ADHD ; however , the routine use of Adderall in larger daily doses poses a significant risk of addiction due to the pronounced reinforcing effects that are present at higher doses .	addiction	addiction	reinforcing effects	reinforcement
Recreational doses of Adderall are generally much larger than prescribed therapeutic doses , and carry a far greater risk of serious adverse effects .

The two amphetamine enantiomers that compose Adderall -LRB- i.e. , levoamphetamine and dextroamphetamine -RRB- alleviate the symptoms of ADHD and narcolepsy by increasing the activity of the neurotransmitters norepinephrine and dopamine in the brain , which results from their interactions with trace amine associated receptor 1 -LRB- TAAR1 -RRB- and vesicular monoamine transporter 2 -LRB- VMAT2 -RRB- in neurons .	amphetamine	amphetamine	narcolepsy	narcolepsy	levoamphetamine	levoamphetamine	dextroamphetamine	dextroamphetamine	norepinephrine	norepinephrine	dopamine	dopamine	brain	human brain	trace amine associated receptor 1	TAAR1	vesicular monoamine transporter 2	vesicular monoamine transporter 2	trace amine	trace amine

Dextroamphetamine is a more potent stimulant than levoamphetamine , but levoamphetamine has slightly stronger cardiovascular and peripheral effects and a longer elimination half-life -LRB- i.e. , it remains in the body longer -RRB- than dextroamphetamine .	stimulant	stimulant	levoamphetamine	levoamphetamine	dextroamphetamine	dextroamphetamine	elimination half-life	elimination half-life

The levoamphetamine component of Adderall has been reported to improve the treatment response in some individuals relative to dextroamphetamine alone .	levoamphetamine	levoamphetamine	dextroamphetamine	dextroamphetamine

Adderall 's active ingredient , amphetamine , shares many chemical and pharmacological properties with the human trace amines , particularly phenethylamine and , the latter of which is a positional isomer of amphetamine .	amphetamine	amphetamine	active ingredient	active ingredient	phenethylamine	phenethylamine	positional isomer	positional isomer
